job.summary: Plan generated and independently checked. Read the findings before assignment.

content.title: Merchant Services Onboarding Plan
content.summary: This onboarding plan covers mandatory and optional learning requirements for a beginner-level Merchant Services employee. Each scheduled module ensures understanding and compliance with company policies on absences, handbook acknowledgment, readiness review, and archive practices within specified stages of employment.

items.source_quote: Employees must acknowledge the current handbook within 1 working day of joining. If access is unavailable, HR records the outage and obtains a supervised paper acknowledgement within the same period.
items.learning_objective: Understand the importance of acknowledging the current employee handbook within 1 working day of joining and the procedures if access is unavailable.
items.practical_activity: Simulate acknowledging the employee handbook electronically. If access is denied, complete a mock supervised paper acknowledgement form and record the outage.
items.lesson: Employees are required to acknowledge the current company handbook within 1 working day of joining. This acknowledgement confirms that the employee has received and reviewed essential policies and procedures. If electronic access to the handbook is unavailable, HR is responsible for recording this outage and ensuring the employee completes a supervised paper-based acknowledgement within the same timeframe. This process ensures compliance and mutual understanding of company expectations from the start.
checklist: Locate and read the current employee handbook.
Acknowledge receipt electronically within 1 working day.
If unable to access electronically, notify HR immediately.
Complete supervised paper acknowledgement with HR if electronic access is unavailable.

scenario.prompt: On your first day, you try to access the employee handbook online but the system is down. How should you proceed to comply with company policy?
scenario.expected_response: You notify HR about the access issue promptly. HR then records the outage and provides a supervised paper acknowledgement form for you to sign within the same 1 working day period.

quiz.question: What should an employee do if they cannot access the employee handbook electronically within 1 working day?
options: Notify HR so they can record the outage and provide a supervised paper acknowledgement.
Wait until the system is available and acknowledge later.
Ignore acknowledgement since access was unavailable.
Send an email to their manager explaining the delay.
quiz.explanation: Employees must acknowledge the current handbook within 1 working day of joining. If access is unavailable, HR records the outage and obtains a supervised paper acknowledgement within the same period.
quiz.evidence_quote: Employees must acknowledge the current handbook within 1 working day of joining. If access is unavailable, HR records the outage and obtains a supervised paper acknowledgement within the same period.

rubric.criterion: Correctly explains the immediate notification and supervised paper acknowledgement procedure.
Completes practical activity by simulating acknowledgement and outage recording.
Demonstrates understanding of timelines and escalation steps in quiz.

items.source_quote: Employees must notify the manager as soon as reasonably possible when an emergency prevents attendance. Where the employee cannot communicate, HR must accept notification from a nominated contact and record the circumstances.
items.learning_objective: Learn the correct procedure for promptly notifying management and HR during emergency absences and the role of nominated contacts.
items.practical_activity: Role-play notifying a manager about an unexpected emergency absence and document notification from a nominated contact if the employee is unavailable.
items.lesson: Employees are obliged to notify their manager as soon as reasonably possible if an emergency prevents their attendance at work. This ensures timely adjustments in staffing and support. If the employee is unable to communicate directly, HR must accept notification from a nominated contact designated by the employee and log the circumstances surrounding the absence. This policy safeguards accurate recording and continuity of operations during unforeseen events.
checklist: Inform your manager immediately when an emergency arises preventing attendance.
If unable to communicate, ensure your nominated contact informs HR promptly.
HR records details of the absence and circumstances.
Follow up with your manager and HR once able to communicate directly.

scenario.prompt: You experience a sudden illness preventing you from attending work and cannot phone your manager. What steps ensure compliance with absence notification policy?
scenario.expected_response: You ask your nominated contact to notify HR about your emergency absence as soon as possible. HR records the situation. Your manager is subsequently informed to manage staffing.

quiz.question: Who can notify HR about an employee's emergency absence if the employee cannot communicate?
options: A nominated contact designated by the employee.
Only the employee themselves.
Any colleague who knows about the absence.
The employee's immediate supervisor.
quiz.explanation: Employees must notify the manager as soon as reasonably possible when an emergency prevents attendance. Where the employee cannot communicate, HR must accept notification from a nominated contact and record the circumstances.
quiz.evidence_quote: Employees must notify the manager as soon as reasonably possible when an emergency prevents attendance. Where the employee cannot communicate, HR must accept notification from a nominated contact and record the circumstances.

rubric.criterion: Accurately explains emergency absence notification and nominated contact role.
Completes practical role-play effectively communicating absence.
Answers quiz correctly demonstrating understanding of notification protocol.

items.source_quote: Managers must review employee readiness by the end of the first 30 calendar days and document remaining gaps, supervised-work limits and follow-up dates.
items.learning_objective: Understand the manager's role in reviewing and documenting employee readiness within the first 30 days, including identifying gaps and setting follow-up plans.
items.practical_activity: Participate in a simulated readiness review where you identify personal skill gaps and propose supervised work limits and follow-up schedules.
items.lesson: Within the first 30 calendar days of employment, managers are required to review each employee's readiness to perform job duties independently. This review includes documenting any remaining training or skill gaps, defining limits on supervised work needed to ensure safety and quality, and scheduling follow-up dates to assess progress. This structured process supports employee development and operational standards.
checklist: Attend the readiness review meeting with your manager.
Discuss current competencies and identify any skills needing improvement.
Agree on supervised work limits necessary while gaps remain.
Set dates for follow-up reviews to monitor progress.

scenario.prompt: During your first month, your manager reviews your readiness and identifies some areas where you need more practice. What should be documented and agreed upon?
scenario.expected_response: The manager documents the remaining skill gaps, sets limits on supervised work, and schedules follow-up dates to track my progress and readiness for full responsibilities.

quiz.question: What must a manager document during the employee readiness review within the first 30 days?
options: Remaining skill gaps, supervised-work limits, and follow-up dates.
Only the employee's strengths and completed tasks.
The employee's attendance record exclusively.
Feedback from other team members.
quiz.explanation: Managers must review employee readiness by the end of the first 30 calendar days and document remaining gaps, supervised-work limits and follow-up dates.
quiz.evidence_quote: Managers must review employee readiness by the end of the first 30 calendar days and document remaining gaps, supervised-work limits and follow-up dates.

rubric.criterion: Identifies and explains required documentation in readiness review.
Actively participates in readiness review simulation, noting gaps and limits.
Correctly answers quiz to demonstrate comprehension of the review requirements.

items.source_quote: Record owners are encouraged to review archive searchability quarterly and propose improvements to naming or indexing.
items.learning_objective: Encourage periodic review of archive searchability and identify ways to improve naming and indexing practices.
items.practical_activity: Conduct a mock quarterly archive review on a sample dataset to identify searchability issues and propose naming or indexing improvements.
items.lesson: Record owners are encouraged to conduct quarterly reviews of archive searchability. This proactive practice helps ensure that records can be accessed efficiently and accurately when needed. During these reviews, owners should analyze the current naming conventions and indexing methods, then propose improvements to streamline retrieval and organization. This continuous improvement supports operational efficiency and compliance with record management standards.
checklist: Schedule quarterly archive searchability reviews.
Evaluate current naming conventions and indexing effectiveness.
Document any issues or inefficiencies discovered.
Propose practical improvements to enhance archive retrieval.

scenario.prompt: You perform a quarterly review of your archive and notice some file names are inconsistent, making searches slow. What steps should you take?
scenario.expected_response: I document the inconsistent naming conventions and suggest standardized naming and indexing improvements to enhance archive searchability for future quarters.

quiz.question: What are record owners encouraged to do quarterly regarding archives?
options: Review archive searchability and propose improvements to naming or indexing.
Delete outdated files to free up space.
Encrypt all archived records for security.
Limit access to archives to managers only.
quiz.explanation: Record owners are encouraged to review archive searchability quarterly and propose improvements to naming or indexing.
quiz.evidence_quote: Record owners are encouraged to review archive searchability quarterly and propose improvements to naming or indexing.

rubric.criterion: Identifies archive issues and proposes concrete naming/indexing improvements.
Completes practical archive review simulation with documentation.
Answers quiz demonstrating understanding of archive review encouragement.

items.source_quote: Employees must store operational evidence in the approved case or document repository. A local copy must not become the sole record of a decision or transaction.
items.module_title: Using Approved Repositories for Operational Evidence
items.learning_objective: Understand the importance of storing operational evidence correctly and learn how to use approved repositories to maintain compliance.
items.practical_activity: Simulate storing a transaction decision document into the approved case repository and verify no sole local copies remain.
items.lesson: Storing operational evidence correctly is essential for legal, audit, and operational integrity. All evidence must be stored in the approved case or document repository to ensure availability and traceability. Keeping only a local copy is not acceptable because it risks loss or lack of accountability. Always upload final and working documents to the approved repository immediately after a transaction or decision is made, making the local copy a temporary aid, not the sole record.
checklist: Identify the approved case or document repository in your system.
Upload a sample operational evidence document to the repository.
Verify the document is accessible and not stored only locally.
Delete or archive local copies after successful upload.

scenario.prompt: You finished a transaction and saved a document related to it on your desktop. What should you do next?
scenario.expected_response: Upload the document into the approved case or document repository so the local copy does not become the sole record.

quiz.question: According to policy, where must employees store operational evidence?
options: In the approved case or document repository
Only as a local copy on their computer
In an email to their manager
On removable external drives only
quiz.explanation: Employees must store operational evidence in the approved case or document repository. A local copy must not become the sole record of a decision or transaction.
quiz.evidence_quote: Employees must store operational evidence in the approved case or document repository. A local copy must not become the sole record of a decision or transaction.

rubric.criterion: Correctly states where operational evidence must be stored
Demonstrates uploading a document to the approved repository
Explains why local copies alone are not permitted

items.source_quote: Employees must stop an unintended transfer where possible and report suspected disclosure through POL-09 immediately. They must preserve evidence and must not conceal or silently delete the incident history.
items.learning_objective: Learn to identify, stop, and report accidental data disclosures while preserving evidence and incident history.
items.practical_activity: Participate in a simulated accidental data transfer scenario to practice stopping transfers, preserving evidence, and submitting a report via the POL-09 process.
items.lesson: If you detect an unintended transfer of sensitive information, you must act immediately to stop it if possible. Reporting suspected disclosures promptly through POL-09 is mandatory to ensure proper investigation and remediation. Always preserve all evidence related to the disclosure and never conceal or delete any incident history silently, as this can impede resolution and may violate policy or laws.
checklist: Recognize signs of accidental data disclosure.
Stop the unintended transfer if it is still possible.
Report the disclosure immediately using the POL-09 process.
Preserve all evidence and incident logs without alteration or deletion.

scenario.prompt: You notice you've accidentally sent sensitive merchant data to the wrong recipient. What steps do you take?
scenario.expected_response: Immediately stop the transfer if possible, report the incident promptly through POL-09, and preserve all evidence and incident history without deleting it.

quiz.question: What must you do after noticing an unintended data transfer?
options: Stop the transfer if possible, report via POL-09 immediately, and preserve evidence
Ignore it if no harm is obvious
Delete the incident history to avoid concern
Report only if a supervisor asks
quiz.explanation: Employees must stop an unintended transfer where possible and report suspected disclosure through POL-09 immediately. They must preserve evidence and must not conceal or silently delete the incident history.
quiz.evidence_quote: Employees must stop an unintended transfer where possible and report suspected disclosure through POL-09 immediately. They must preserve evidence and must not conceal or silently delete the incident history.

rubric.criterion: Correctly identifies steps to stop and report data disclosure
Preserves evidence and incident history in practice
Reports incident through the proper POL-09 channel

items.source_quote: The Merchant Success Executive must review open merchant issues at least weekly and record the accountable owner and next action for each unresolved issue.
items.module_title: Weekly Review of Open Merchant Issues
items.learning_objective: Develop skills to conduct weekly reviews of open merchant issues by identifying owners and defining next actions.
items.practical_activity: Complete a simulated review of a list of merchant issues, update issue log with accountable owners and next steps for unresolved cases.
items.lesson: As a Merchant Success Executive, you are required to review all open merchant issues at least once per week to ensure progress and accountability. For each unresolved issue, you must record the accountable owner responsible for resolution and clearly define the next action required. This process helps maintain issue visibility, improves communication among stakeholders, and accelerates timely resolution.
checklist: Access the current list of open merchant issues.
For each unresolved issue, identify and record the accountable owner.
Define and document the next action for each open issue.
Update the issue log and communicate updates as needed.

scenario.prompt: During your weekly review, you find several unresolved issues without owners or next steps. What should you do?
scenario.expected_response: Assign an accountable owner and define the next action for each unresolved issue to ensure they are actively managed.

quiz.question: What must be recorded during your weekly review of open merchant issues?
options: The accountable owner and next action for each unresolved issue
Only the issue description
The total number of issues without details
Only issues resolved that week
quiz.explanation: The Merchant Success Executive must review open merchant issues at least weekly and record the accountable owner and next action for each unresolved issue.
quiz.evidence_quote: The Merchant Success Executive must review open merchant issues at least weekly and record the accountable owner and next action for each unresolved issue.

rubric.criterion: Accurately identifies accountable owners for each issue
Documents appropriate next actions for unresolved issues
Completes and updates issue log correctly

items.source_quote: Employees must communicate respectfully and must not harass, threaten or discriminate against another person. A witness must report concerns through the confidential HR channel without circulating the allegation to colleagues.
items.learning_objective: Understand and apply respectful communication standards and appropriate reporting channels for concerns about harassment or discrimination.
items.practical_activity: Review a series of workplace scenarios to identify respectful vs. disrespectful communication and practice submitting a confidential HR report correctly without sharing allegations with colleagues.
items.lesson: Respectful communication is a mandatory standard. Employees must not harass, threaten, or discriminate against others. Any concerns witnessed must be reported through the confidential HR channel to protect privacy and ensure proper investigation. Circulating allegations among colleagues is prohibited to prevent gossip, retaliation, or misinformation. Always maintain professionalism and confidentiality when addressing workplace conduct issues.
checklist: Communicate clearly and respectfully in all interactions.
Recognize behaviors that constitute harassment, threats, or discrimination.
If witnessing misconduct, use the confidential HR reporting channel.
Avoid sharing or discussing allegations publicly among colleagues.

scenario.prompt: You hear a colleague make a discriminatory remark in a meeting. What is the appropriate action?
scenario.expected_response: Report the concern privately through the confidential HR channel and do not discuss the allegation with other colleagues.

quiz.question: How should employees report witnessed harassment or discrimination?
options: Through the confidential HR channel without circulating the allegation
By telling all their colleagues promptly
Ignore it to avoid conflict
Report directly to the harasser’s manager only
quiz.explanation: Employees must communicate respectfully and must not harass, threaten or discriminate against another person. A witness must report concerns through the confidential HR channel without circulating the allegation to colleagues.
quiz.evidence_quote: Employees must communicate respectfully and must not harass, threaten or discriminate against another person. A witness must report concerns through the confidential HR channel without circulating the allegation to colleagues.

rubric.criterion: Identifies appropriate respectful behaviors
Demonstrates correct confidential reporting procedure
Avoids improper sharing of allegations with colleagues

items.source_quote: Employees must score at least 80 percent on mandatory knowledge assessments. A failed attempt requires targeted revision and another attempt; the original result must remain recorded.
items.learning_objective: Ensure the employee achieves at least an 80% score on mandatory assessments to demonstrate essential knowledge.
items.practical_activity: Complete the mandatory knowledge assessment covering key Merchant Services policies and procedures. If scoring below 80%, review the provided revision materials and retake the assessment.
items.lesson: Employees must achieve a minimum score of 80 percent on mandatory knowledge assessments to confirm their understanding of essential policies and procedures. If an employee does not meet this threshold on the first attempt, they must undertake targeted revision focusing on weak areas and then retake the assessment. Note that all original attempts and scores are retained in records for compliance tracking.
checklist: Review all mandatory assessment topics thoroughly.
Take the initial knowledge assessment when scheduled.
If score is below 80%, complete targeted revision using provided resources.
Retake the assessment until scoring at least 80%.

scenario.prompt: You scored 75% on your first mandatory knowledge assessment.
scenario.expected_response: I will review the assessment results to identify weak topics, complete the targeted revision materials provided, and then schedule and retake the assessment to achieve at least an 80% score. I understand my initial score will remain recorded.

quiz.question: What must an employee do if they score below 80% on a mandatory knowledge assessment?
options: Undertake targeted revision and retake the assessment with original results recorded.
Skip revision and proceed with job duties.
Request to skip the assessment entirely.
Retake the assessment without any revision.
quiz.explanation: Employees must score at least 80 percent on mandatory knowledge assessments. A failed attempt requires targeted revision and another attempt; the original result must remain recorded.
quiz.evidence_quote: Employees must score at least 80 percent on mandatory knowledge assessments. A failed attempt requires targeted revision and another attempt; the original result must remain recorded.

rubric.criterion: Identifies need for revision after low score on assessment
Completes targeted revision before retaking assessment
Scores at least 80% on reassessment

items.source_quote: Employees must request correction of an inaccurate attendance entry within 2 working days of discovering it. HR must retain the original value and the evidence supporting correction.
items.learning_objective: Learn to identify and report inaccurate attendance entries promptly to ensure accurate HR records.
items.practical_activity: Simulate identifying an inaccurate attendance record and submit a correction request within 2 working days using the company HR portal, including supporting evidence.
items.lesson: Employees are required to request corrections for any inaccurate attendance entries within 2 working days of discovering the error. This ensures timely and accurate record-keeping. Human Resources (HR) is responsible for retaining the original attendance value and any evidence supporting the correction, maintaining audit trails and compliance.
checklist: Review your attendance entries regularly for accuracy.
If an inaccuracy is found, gather evidence supporting the correction.
Submit a correction request to HR within 2 working days of discovery.
Retain copies of all communication and evidence submitted.

scenario.prompt: You notice your attendance record shows you arrived an hour later than you actually did two days ago.
scenario.expected_response: I will gather any supporting evidence such as badge swipe logs or supervisor confirmation, and submit a correction request to HR immediately, ensuring this is done within 2 working days of discovering the error.

quiz.question: Within what timeframe must employees request a correction for an inaccurate attendance entry after discovering it?
options: 2 working days
1 week
Immediately with no deadline
5 working days
quiz.explanation: Employees must request correction of an inaccurate attendance entry within 2 working days of discovering it. HR must retain the original value and the evidence supporting correction.
quiz.evidence_quote: Employees must request correction of an inaccurate attendance entry within 2 working days of discovering it. HR must retain the original value and the evidence supporting correction.

rubric.criterion: Identifies the inaccuracy and evidence required
Submits correction request within 2 working days
Includes proper documentation supporting the correction

items.source_quote: Document owners must link each revision to the superseded version and identify changed sections. Employees must use the version effective on the date of the activity; historical copies remain available for audit.
items.learning_objective: Understand how to use current document versions and track revisions to maintain compliance.
items.practical_activity: Practice reviewing document versions, identify changes from the previous version, and verify the effective version to use for a simulated operational task on a specific date.
items.lesson: Document owners are responsible for linking each revision of a document to its superseded version and clearly identifying the sections that have changed. Employees must always use the document version that was effective on the date they perform an activity or task, ensuring compliance with current policies at that time. Historical copies of documents remain accessible for audit and reference purposes.
checklist: Check document revision history before use.
Verify the version effective as of the activity date.
Identify any changes since the previous version linked.
Use the correct version for work and retain access to historical versions for audits.

scenario.prompt: You must complete a process that started last week. You have found two versions of the procedure document: one revised yesterday and one from two weeks ago.
scenario.expected_response: I will use the document version that was effective on the date the process started (two weeks ago), review the revision notes linking it to prior versions, and ensure any changes in the newer version are understood for future processes but not applied retroactively.

quiz.question: Which document version should you use to perform an activity dated last week?
options: The version effective on the date of the activity
The latest available version
The earliest version in the archive
Any version with the most changes
quiz.explanation: Document owners must link each revision to the superseded version and identify changed sections. Employees must use the version effective on the date of the activity; historical copies remain available for audit.
quiz.evidence_quote: Document owners must link each revision to the superseded version and identify changed sections. Employees must use the version effective on the date of the activity; historical copies remain available for audit.

rubric.criterion: Correctly identifies the effective version based on activity date
Demonstrates understanding of linking revisions
Uses historical versions appropriately for audit or reference

items.source_quote: The duty Operations Manager must appoint an incident lead and record the handover. IT leads technical containment while the incident lead coordinates business decisions and communications.
items.learning_objective: Understand the roles in incident management including appointment and responsibilities of the incident lead and IT technical lead.
items.practical_activity: Simulate an incident scenario, appoint an incident lead, document the handover, and coordinate with IT for technical containment and business communication.
items.lesson: During an incident, the duty Operations Manager is required to appoint an incident lead and formally record the handover of responsibility. While the IT team leads the technical containment efforts of the incident, the incident lead is responsible for coordinating all business-related decisions and communications. This separation of roles ensures clear accountability and effective management during incidents.
checklist: Operations Manager appoints an incident lead promptly upon incident discovery.
Document the handover details clearly.
Coordinate with IT to lead technical containment.
Incident lead manages business decisions and communications.

scenario.prompt: A security breach is detected. As Operations Manager, how do you manage incident leadership?
scenario.expected_response: I appoint an incident lead immediately and document the handover clearly. I ensure IT takes charge of technical containment while the incident lead coordinates all business decisions and communications with stakeholders.

quiz.question: Who coordinates business decisions and communications during an incident?
options: The incident lead
The duty Operations Manager
The IT technical lead
The security officer
quiz.explanation: The duty Operations Manager must appoint an incident lead and record the handover. IT leads technical containment while the incident lead coordinates business decisions and communications.
quiz.evidence_quote: The duty Operations Manager must appoint an incident lead and record the handover. IT leads technical containment while the incident lead coordinates business decisions and communications.

rubric.criterion: Appoints incident lead and documents handover correctly
Distinguishes roles of IT lead vs. incident lead
Effectively manages communication and coordination during incident

items.source_quote: Employees must delete approved temporary customer-data exports within 24 elapsed hours after the approved task ends. A documented preservation hold suspends deletion only for the records identified in that hold.
items.learning_objective: Understand and perform deletion of approved temporary customer-data exports within the required 24-hour timeframe unless suspended by a preservation hold.
items.practical_activity: Simulate completing an approved temporary customer-data export task and record the timing to delete the export within 24 hours in the system's test environment. Identify and apply a preservation hold on specific records.
items.lesson: Employees must delete approved temporary customer-data exports within 24 elapsed hours after the approved task ends. This means immediately scheduling deletion tasks to avoid overdue data presence. However, if a documented preservation hold exists, deletion is suspended only for the records explicitly identified in the hold, ensuring data is retained lawfully. Timely and accurate removal protects customer privacy and compliance.
checklist: Verify export task approval and completion timestamp
Confirm no applicable preservation hold exists or identify records under hold
Schedule and perform deletion of temporary data within 24 elapsed hours
Document deletion completion and hold status accordingly

scenario.prompt: You have just completed a customer data export task approved by your manager. How do you ensure compliance with data export deletion requirements?
scenario.expected_response: I check if the export task is complete, verify if any preservation holds apply, and delete the temporary export data within 24 elapsed hours after task completion, except for records under a documented hold.

quiz.question: What is the required timeframe to delete approved temporary customer-data exports after task completion?
options: Within 24 elapsed hours after the approved task ends
Within 48 working hours after task completion
Within 1 week of task completion
Only when requested by a manager
quiz.explanation: Employees must delete approved temporary customer-data exports within 24 elapsed hours after the approved task ends, ensuring timely removal and compliance. Preservation holds suspend deletion only for specified records.
quiz.evidence_quote: Employees must delete approved temporary customer-data exports within 24 elapsed hours after the approved task ends. A documented preservation hold suspends deletion only for the records identified in that hold.

rubric.criterion: Accurately identifies deletion timeframe and preservation hold rules
Successfully completes the simulated deletion within 24 hours
Documents preservation hold correctly during practical activity

items.source_quote: Employees must complete the relevant prerequisite training before independently performing restricted tasks. A manager may arrange supervised practice but must not mark an unmet prerequisite complete.
items.module_title: Completing Prerequisite Training for Restricted Tasks
items.learning_objective: Learn the importance of completing prerequisite training before independently performing restricted tasks and procedures for supervised practice arrangements.
items.practical_activity: Review a list of restricted tasks and their prerequisite trainings, then plan a supervised practice session with a manager for one restricted task without marking the prerequisite as complete prematurely.
items.lesson: Employees must complete the relevant prerequisite training before independently performing restricted tasks to ensure safety and competence. Managers may arrange supervised practice opportunities to build skills, but they must not mark an unmet prerequisite training as complete. This policy maintains training integrity and ensures employees are fully prepared before independent work on restricted tasks.
checklist: Identify restricted tasks assigned to your role
Verify completion status of all prerequisite trainings
Coordinate a supervised practice session with your manager for restricted tasks
Avoid marking prerequisites as complete without successful training

scenario.prompt: You are assigned a restricted task but have not completed its prerequisite training. What steps should you take?
scenario.expected_response: I will complete the required prerequisite training first. If allowed, I will request supervised practice arranged by my manager but will not mark the prerequisite training as complete before finishing it.

quiz.question: What is true about prerequisite training for restricted tasks?
options: Must be completed before independent performance; supervised practice can be arranged but prerequisites are not marked complete until finished
Prerequisites can be marked complete after supervised practice without formal training
Employees can skip prerequisite training if supervised practice is arranged
Managers can mark prerequisite training complete at their discretion
quiz.explanation: Prerequisite training must be completed before independent performance. Managers may arrange supervised practice but cannot mark unmet prerequisites as complete to ensure full compliance.
quiz.evidence_quote: Employees must complete the relevant prerequisite training before independently performing restricted tasks. A manager may arrange supervised practice but must not mark an unmet prerequisite complete.

rubric.criterion: Correctly explains requirement for prerequisite completion
Plans supervised practice without prematurely marking completion
Demonstrates understanding of training and task assignment process

items.source_quote: Employees must assess parcel weight and route before lifting and must request approved handling assistance when the posted safe-handling limit is exceeded. They must not invent a universal weight limit where a task assessment is required.
items.learning_objective: Learn to assess parcel weight and route before lifting and request approved assistance when exceeding safe-handling limits without inventing universal limits.
items.practical_activity: Perform a simulated assessment of several parcels with varying weights and routes, deciding when to request handling assistance according to posted limits, and document decisions accordingly.
items.lesson: Employees must assess each parcel's weight and delivery route before lifting. When a parcel's weight exceeds posted safe-handling limits, employees must request approved handling assistance. Importantly, employees must not invent a universal weight limit, as each task requires its own assessment to ensure safety and compliance with handling policies.
checklist: Check the posted safe-handling weight limit for parcels
Assess weight and route of parcels before attempting to lift
Request approved assistance if parcel weight exceeds posted limit
Avoid using invented or assumed weight limits without proper assessment

scenario.prompt: You are assigned to lift parcels for delivery. One parcel appears heavy, but no universal weight limit is posted. What do you do?
scenario.expected_response: I assess the actual parcel weight and delivery route. If the weight exceeds the posted safe-handling limit for that parcel, I request approved handling assistance. I do not rely on any invented universal weight limit.

quiz.question: What should employees do when lifting parcels according to the safe manual handling policy?
options: Assess each parcel's weight and route and request assistance if over the posted safe-handling limit
Use a universal weight limit for all parcels when deciding assistance needs
Lift all parcels unless obviously dangerous without assessment
Request assistance only if a supervisor tells you to
quiz.explanation: Employees must assess parcel weight and route before lifting and request approved assistance when exceeding the posted safe-handling limit. They must not invent a universal weight limit where assessment is required.
quiz.evidence_quote: Employees must assess parcel weight and route before lifting and must request approved handling assistance when the posted safe-handling limit is exceeded. They must not invent a universal weight limit where a task assessment is required.

rubric.criterion: Correctly identifies when to request handling assistance
Performs assessment without inventing universal limits
Documents parcel assessments accurately during practical activity

items.source_quote: Employees must demonstrate the critical steps of a role task to an authorized assessor before independent work. A numerical score cannot compensate for a failed safety or privacy critical step.
items.module_title: Demonstrating Practical Competence for Role Tasks
items.learning_objective: Master the critical safety and privacy steps of assigned role tasks and successfully demonstrate them to an authorized assessor before working independently.
items.practical_activity: Prepare and perform a demonstration of all critical steps in a key role task for an authorized assessor, emphasizing safety and privacy procedures, and receive feedback.
items.lesson: Employees must demonstrate all critical steps of a role task to an authorized assessor before working independently. This ensures that safety and privacy requirements are met and protects both employees and customers. Numerical scoring alone is insufficient; failure at any critical safety or privacy step means the demonstration is failed, emphasizing the importance of full compliance.
checklist: Identify critical safety and privacy steps within your role task
Practice the full sequence of steps thoroughly
Schedule and perform a demonstration with an authorized assessor
Correct any failed steps and repeat the demonstration if necessary

scenario.prompt: Before starting independent work, your assessor indicates you missed a critical safety step. How do you respond?
scenario.expected_response: I acknowledge the failure, review the critical safety step thoroughly, practice it again, and schedule another demonstration to ensure full compliance before working independently.

quiz.question: Why can a numerical score not compensate for failing a critical safety or privacy step in a role task demonstration?
options: Because critical steps must be performed correctly to ensure safety and privacy regardless of overall score
Because numerical scores reflect only efficiency, not compliance
Because failing steps can be overlooked if the score is high enough
Because assessors do not consider critical steps in evaluations
quiz.explanation: A numerical score cannot compensate for failing any critical safety or privacy step since these steps are essential for safe and compliant task performance.
quiz.evidence_quote: Employees must demonstrate the critical steps of a role task to an authorized assessor before independent work. A numerical score cannot compensate for a failed safety or privacy critical step.

rubric.criterion: Accurately demonstrates all critical safety and privacy steps
Effectively responds and corrects any failed steps
Shows readiness for independent work post-assessment

items.source_quote: Employees must verify the requester using the approved workflow before disclosing shipment details. A shipment number alone does not authorize disclosure of the recipient address or contact details.
items.learning_objective: Understand and apply the approved workflow to verify requesters before disclosing shipment recipient details, safeguarding sensitive information.
items.practical_activity: Simulate a request for shipment details from a customer service inquiry. Use the approved workflow to verify the requester’s identity before providing any recipient contact information.
items.lesson: Employees must always verify the requester using the approved workflow before disclosing shipment details. items.source_quote: Employees must follow the latest effective approved policy, then the applicable SOP, then an approved role guide, then an FAQ. A lower-authority document cannot override a policy; unresolved conflicts go to the policy owner before action.
items.learning_objective: Understand and apply the order of precedence among company policy documents when performing tasks.
items.practical_activity: Review sample conflict scenarios between policy documents and determine appropriate escalation steps.
items.lesson: When performing your work, you must always follow the latest effective approved company policy first. If no policy applies, follow the applicable Standard Operating Procedure (SOP). If you find conflicts or unclear instructions between these documents, escalate the issue to the policy owner before proceeding. This ensures compliance and avoids operational errors.

Refer to approved role guides and FAQs if further guidance is needed.
Report unresolved conflicts between documents to the policy owner for clarification.

Prepare and submit a notification record as soon as practical after initial response.

requirements.text: Document owners must record document ID, owner, version, approval role and effective date before release. An unapproved draft must not be used to assign mandatory training.
requirements.title: Controlled copies

requirements.text: Employees must use only the approved numbered fallback forms or controlled offline register during an outage. Personal notebooks and unapproved messaging groups must not hold customer records.
requirements.title: Approved fallback

requirements.text: The Merchant Success Executive must brief the merchant on the approved prohibited-item list and escalation route before the first shipment. Unlisted uncertain items require Operations Manager review.
requirements.title: Explain prohibited items

requirements.text: Employees must report suspicious links, attachments or unexpected authentication requests to IT without opening them. If already opened, the employee must report the action and follow the incident process in POL-09.
requirements.title: Suspicious content

requirements.text: Employees must lock an unattended workstation immediately and configure automatic locking after no more than 5 minutes of inactivity. Shared warehouse terminals follow the same limit.
requirements.title: Screen lock

requirements.text: Only the duty Operations Manager may activate the continuity procedure after assessing service impact. If immediate danger exists, employees must take the safety actions in POL-08 without waiting for activation.
requirements.title: Continuity activation

requirements.text: Employees must submit a planned absence request at least 3 working days before the proposed start. The manager may approve shorter notice only after recording a coverage arrangement.
requirements.title: Planned absence notice

requirements.text: Managers must not disadvantage a person for raising a good-faith concern or participating in an investigation. Any alleged retaliation must be referred to the Managing Director.
requirements.title: Non retaliation

requirements.text: Employees must stop work and use the signed evacuation route when the alarm sounds. They must report to the assembly point and must not re-enter until the incident lead authorizes it.
requirements.title: Emergency evacuation

requirements.text: Employees hosting a visitor must arrange registration, a visible visitor pass and an escort in restricted areas. Visitors must not use employee access credentials.
requirements.title: Visitor escort

requirements.text: Employees must log access, correction or deletion requests and refer them to the Operations Manager on the same working day. Employees must not promise deletion before checking preservation requirements.
requirements.title: Privacy requests

requirements.text: Employees must record only shipment ID, action, time and assigned operator in the fallback register. Additional personal data requires explicit incident-lead approval and privacy controls.
requirements.title: Minimum fallback data

requirements.text: Employees are encouraged to complete optional phishing simulations and discuss the warning signs with IT after the exercise.
requirements.title: Security practice

requirements.text: Employees must not operate powered warehouse equipment without documented authorization and task-specific training. Observing another operator does not grant authorization.
requirements.title: Restricted equipment

requirements.text: HR must retain onboarding acknowledgements, assessment attempts and readiness decisions for 24 months after the employee leaves the company, unless a preservation hold applies.
requirements.title: Training retention

requirements.text: Employees must use company-managed devices or an explicitly approved device profile to access restricted data. Personal storage services must not receive company files.
requirements.title: Approved devices

requirements.text: Employees must transfer open tasks, critical deadlines and escalation contacts to the designated cover before planned absence. Customer personal data must remain in approved systems.
requirements.title: Shift handover

requirements.text: Employees may propose a simpler fallback step after a rehearsal, provided the proposal preserves privacy, traceability and independent approval.
requirements.title: Continuity improvements

requirements.text: Employees must declare any offered gift valued above PKR 1,000 to HR before accepting it. Cash and cash-equivalent gifts are prohibited at any value; splitting a gift does not avoid this rule.
requirements.title: Gift declaration

requirements.text: Assigned record owners must reconcile fallback entries within 1 working day of restoration, resolve mismatches and dispose of temporary copies according to POL-06 and POL-07.
requirements.title: Fallback reconciliation

requirements.text: Employees must use fictional or irreversibly anonymized customer examples in training and demonstrations. Replacing a name alone does not anonymize a record containing a real telephone number or address.
requirements.title: Training data

requirements.text: Employees must obtain Managing Director approval before representing the company publicly or publishing customer-related material. Personal accounts must not disclose internal records.
requirements.title: Public statements

requirements.text: Employees must record actual events and must not fabricate delivery attempts, training completion, assessment results or approvals. Corrections must retain the original entry and the reason for amendment.
requirements.title: Accurate records

requirements.text: Responders must preserve relevant logs, messages and event identifiers without modifying originals. Evidence access must be restricted to the response team and a preservation hold applied where necessary.
requirements.title: Evidence preservation

requirements.text: Employees must use the confidential HR channel to report misconduct. If the concern involves HR, the report must go directly to the Managing Director.
requirements.title: Confidential reporting

requirements.text: Employees must obtain recorded approval before taking planned leave. Submission alone is not approval, and employees must not approve their own request.
requirements.title: Approval before absence

requirements.text: Employees may select an optional development topic after agreeing the time allocation with their manager; optional learning must not delay mandatory training.
requirements.title: Personal development

requirements.text: Employees must transfer personal data only through approved company systems to authorized recipients. Personal messaging accounts and publicly accessible links are prohibited.
requirements.title: Approved transfer

requirements.text: The Merchant Success Executive must refer requests to change settlement details to Finance verification and must not update bank details on an email instruction alone.
requirements.title: Protect payment changes

requirements.text: Record owners must retain routine delivery-event records for 180 calendar days after case closure. A documented preservation hold overrides routine deletion until the hold is formally released.
requirements.title: Routine operational retention

requirements.text: Employees must refer records with no applicable retention category to the Operations Manager before deletion. They must not infer a deadline from an unrelated record type.
requirements.title: Retention uncertainty

requirements.text: Teams are encouraged to rehearse one incident scenario each month and document a specific improvement to the response procedure.
requirements.title: Response rehearsal

requirements.text: HR must assign an onboarding plan based on role, experience, location and applicable requirements. Prior experience may change practice difficulty but must not remove mandatory acknowledgements.
requirements.title: Individual plan

requirements.text: Employees must access and collect only the customer fields needed for an assigned task. Full identity documents must not be requested for routine parcel tracking.
requirements.title: Minimum necessary data

requirements.text: The first available responder must create an incident record containing observed facts, discovery time, affected services and initial actions. Speculation must be labelled and credentials must be excluded.
requirements.title: Incident record

requirements.text: During an activated continuity event, the incident lead must issue an internal status checkpoint at least every 30 elapsed minutes until normal service resumes. A checkpoint must state current impact, owner and next update time.
requirements.title: Outage checkpoints

requirements.text: Record owners must correct errors through an auditable amendment recording author, time and reason. Original transaction values must not be overwritten without history.
requirements.title: Record correction

requirements.text: Employees must pause the affected activity and ask the document owner when two equally authoritative instructions conflict or a necessary limit is missing. The owner must record the resolution before work resumes.
requirements.title: Unclear requirements

requirements.text: Employees are encouraged to discuss anticipated leave early so teams can plan coverage before a formal request is submitted.
requirements.title: Calendar planning

requirements.text: Managers must confirm required operational coverage before approving concurrent absences. If coverage cannot be arranged, the manager must record the reason and discuss alternative dates.
requirements.title: Minimum coverage

requirements.text: Employees must activate multifactor authentication before accessing email, remote access or systems holding customer records. IT must provide an approved recovery method rather than disabling the requirement.
requirements.title: Multifactor authentication

requirements.text: Record owners must use approved disposal methods and retain a disposal log identifying category, date range, authorization and completion date. Disposal must not expose readable personal data.
requirements.title: Secure disposal

requirements.text: The Merchant Success Executive must coordinate a supervised first-shipment check with Dispatch and confirm identifiers, labels and contacts before routine volume is accepted.
requirements.title: Coordinate first shipment

requirements.text: Employees must disclose a personal or financial relationship with a merchant or supplier before participating in its selection, payment or complaint decision. The manager must assign an independent decision-maker.
requirements.title: Personal interests

requirements.text: Employees are encouraged to suggest improvements to workstation layout or parcel movement after discussing them with the supervisor.
requirements.title: Safety suggestions

requirements.text: Reviewers must verify required evidence before recording completion. Reading a module alone does not demonstrate practical competence or substitute for a required policy acknowledgement.
requirements.title: Completion integrity

requirements.text: Employees must record near misses even when no injury or damage occurs. The supervisor must assign a corrective action owner and verify completion.
requirements.title: Near misses

requirements.text: HR must record each employee role, department, joining date and reporting manager before assigning onboarding. A temporary role change requires a recorded start date, end date and additional requirements.
requirements.title: Role assignment

requirements.text: The incident lead must obtain an IT health check and an operational sample check before declaring normal service restored. A login screen alone is not evidence of end-to-end recovery.
requirements.title: Recovery verification

requirements.text: Employees must obtain IT approval before installing software or browser extensions on company devices. IT must verify business purpose and permitted access before approval.
requirements.title: Software installation

requirements.text: Employees entering marked warehouse handling zones must wear the posted protective equipment. The supervisor must stop the task if suitable equipment is unavailable.
requirements.title: Personal protective equipment

requirements.text: Employees must store API keys and service credentials only in approved secret storage and must not include them in source repositories, screenshots, training examples or support tickets.
requirements.title: Secrets handling

requirements.text: The Merchant Success Executive must record agreed service zones, cutoffs, return conditions and billing terms in the approved agreement. Oral promises must not alter recorded terms.
requirements.title: Record service terms

requirements.text: Only the incident lead or a designated spokesperson may issue incident updates to merchants or customers. Updates must distinguish confirmed impact from investigation assumptions.
requirements.title: External communication

requirements.text: Employees may suggest removal of unnecessary personal-data fields from forms, reports or dashboards to the relevant process owner.
requirements.title: Privacy improvements

requirements.text: Employees must classify an incident as critical when it involves immediate physical danger, suspected exposure of customer data or complete loss of dispatch capability. Where severity is uncertain, they must escalate as critical pending review.
requirements.title: Severity classification

requirements.text: Employees must check shipment and transaction identifiers before entering recovered work into the restored system. Potential duplicates must be held for review rather than posted again.
requirements.title: Duplicate prevention

requirements.text: The Merchant Success Executive may provide a monthly service-improvement summary based on approved aggregated performance data.
requirements.title: Share improvement insights

requirements.text: Training managers must distribute learning across Day 1, Week 1, Week 2 and First 30 Days. Mandatory operational deadlines and prerequisites take priority over a convenient stage label.
requirements.title: Learning stages

requirements.text: Employees must report a non-urgent safety concern before the end of the current shift. An immediate danger requires stopping the activity and alerting the shift supervisor at once.
requirements.title: Safety concern reporting

requirements.text: HR must restrict medical or other sensitive absence details to authorized People Operations staff. Operational managers receive only information needed to arrange work.
requirements.title: Sensitive absence details

requirements.text: The Operations Manager must identify scope, owner and start date when issuing a preservation hold. Record owners must suspend scheduled deletion for the named records until written release.
requirements.title: Preservation holds

requirements.text: The Merchant Success Executive must complete the approved merchant profile and verification checklist before activation. Missing verification evidence requires a hold and manager review.
requirements.title: Verify merchant onboarding

requirements.text: Employees are encouraged to arrange a weekly discussion with an experienced colleague during the first month to clarify workflows and identify useful practice.
requirements.title: Onboarding buddy

requirements.text: The incident lead must record recovery evidence, outstanding risks and corrective action owners before closure. The Operations Manager must review critical incidents within 2 working days after restoration.
requirements.title: Incident closure

requirements.text: Employees must use individually assigned accounts and must not share passwords or authentication codes. Service accounts require a named IT owner and must not be used for routine interactive work.
requirements.title: Individual accounts

requirements.text: Employees must follow the latest effective approved policy, then the applicable SOP, then an approved role guide, then an FAQ. A lower-authority document cannot override a policy; unresolved conflicts go to the policy owner before action.
requirements.title: Authoritative instructions

requirements.text: Employees must notify the duty Operations Manager within 15 elapsed minutes of discovering a critical incident. Immediate emergency or containment actions must not wait for a ticket; the notification record must follow as soon as practical.
requirements.title: Critical escalation

requirements.text: Employees must complete core orientation within 2 working days of joining. HR must schedule a replacement session within that deadline if the original session is cancelled.
requirements.title: Core orientation
